$comment: CANONICAL emoji -> icon name. The migration's single source of truth.
This exists so `📋` resolves to `clipboard` in every repo instead of `clipboard`
in one and `paste` in the next. Twelve repos migrating independently would each
re-decide these, and the drift would be invisible until two apps sat side by side
on the frontpage showing different glyphs for the same idea.
`check-icons` reads this to SUGGEST the replacement in its findings, which is what
turns each one from a decision into an edit. Keys are matched with variation
selectors stripped, so `⚙` and `⚙️` both land on `gear`.
Every value must exist in sources.json — check-icons fails loudly if one does not.
$comment_ambiguous: A FLAT MAP CANNOT RESOLVE THESE. One emoji, two right answers depending on what
sits next to it, so `$ambiguous` names them and both tools defer to a human:
the codemod refuses them outright, and check-icons prints the caveat under its
suggestion instead of presenting one arm of a pair as settled.
`◀`/`▶` is the case that proved it. `▶` lives in the transport row below with
`⏸`/`⏭`/`⏮` because a play button really is `play` — hadoku-dataplatform's
But `◀`/`▶` is just as often a mirrored nav pair, and there applying the map
arm by arm yields an outline chevron facing a filled triangle. That is exactly
how promptsmith shipped a mismatched tournament row, and how the same repo's
PartBadge `◀ ▶` had to be hand-corrected to chevron-left/chevron-right.
Neither value can move without breaking the other site, so the ambiguity is
recorded here rather than papered over with a coin-flip default.

$ambiguous.◀: in a mirrored `◀ … ▶` pair use chevron-left WITH chevron-right — never pair it with play
$ambiguous.▶: play ONLY as a transport control beside ⏸; in a mirrored `◀ … ▶` pair use chevron-right
